title: Chapter 21: Demonic Tag at Twilight
content:
Chapter 21:

Demonic Tag at Twilight

In that instant, the only thing dominating Subaru’s mind was a complete blank.

He couldn’t even conjure a clinging plea to deny the spectacle before his eyes. Subaru’s thoughts were simply, utterly buried in a landscape of white.

A stagnation, as if his throat had frozen, his breathing forgotten, his very heart stopped. What broke the spell was the sensation of a single drop of sweat caressing his skin as it trickled down his forehead.

With the feeling of the sweat dripping from his chin to the ground, Subaru’s consciousness returned from the void.

However, facing reality meant there was no denying that the person standing before him was the one person he hadn’t wanted to believe was there.

—This is bad. Badbadbadbadbadbad.

Following the blankness, what filled his thoughts was a chaotic litany born of impatience and confusion.

He couldn’t think straight. Was the person standing before him really the Rem that Subaru knew? Or could it be an impostor? No, there was no possibility of an impostor. There was no point in doing such a thing.

“Maybe you’re actually triplets…”

Subaru himself knew best that even if that were true, it would offer no comfort at all.

Watching Subaru, whose fighting spirit had evaporated, Rem gently stroked her short blue hair with her free hand.

“If you do not resist, Rem will make the end painless.”

“Do you really think there’s a human alive who’d hear that offer and say, ‘Yes, that’s right, please do, hihihi!’?”

“Rem apologizes. You are right; you were indeed that sort of person, esteemed guest.”

The way she bowed so politely was far too divorced from the atmosphere of the scene. Her demeanor was so unchanged from her usual self that one might mistake this for a casual scene inside the mansion.

That only made the alien presence of the rugged weapon gripped in her hand all the more tremendous.

“A girl wielding a savage weapon is definitely a romantic trope, but…”

An iron chain and a spiked iron ball—a lethal blunt weapon that would mince anyone it hit directly. The gentleman who chose this for her must have had terribly bad taste.

Subaru had already tasted its power once and had his life scattered by it. He knew from firsthand experience that she could manipulate it at will.

Involuntarily swallowing his breath, turning his panic into drops on his forehead, he formed words.

“Can I say a cliché line like… ‘Why are you doing this?’”

“It is not that difficult. Punish the suspicious. It is a maids duty.”

“Don’t you have the phrase ‘Love thy neighbor’?”

“Rem’s hands are already full.”

Perhaps she had no intention of playing along with his stalling; Rem’s gaze never once softened as she answered him.

He couldn’t read her next move. But there was one thing he did know.

That if he moved now, he would definitely die.

Subaru’s instincts, having died five times in one way or another, were screaming that alert at him.

It was too one-sided a checkmate to call it a stalemate. Subaru spun his wheels frantically, struggling to squeeze out even a little bit of information.

He had to avoid stepping on a landmine, pique her interest, and drag out the conversation. telling himself this, Subaru tried to avert his eyes, if only temporarily, from the despairing fact closing in on him.

Because if he faced it head-on, he wouldn’t be able to stop himself from collapsing to his knees.

“—Does Ram know about this?”

The name that slipped out of his mouth was that of the older sister who looked exactly like her.

Unfriendly, foul-mouthed, with a bad attitude, and maid skills that fell short of her sister’s across the board—a hopeless stat sheet—but she was the one Subaru had spent the most total days with at the Roswaal Manor.

If even that girl, with whom he had enjoyed bickering, had turned into Subaru’s enemy—just the thought made his body tremble. But,

“Rem intends to finish this before Sister sees.”

The answer Rem gave was, unintentionally, the very answer Subaru had been seeking.

The situation remained bad, but he was saved from plunging into the absolute worst mood just in the nick of time.

He let out a long breath, surprised that it came from relief.

To find something to be optimistic about in such a cornered situation—just how lukewarm was his way of thinking?

Raising his head, Subaru looked straight back into Rem’s eyes. And, watching Rem furrow her brows slightly at his glare,

“So, you’re acting on your own? Not following Roswaal’s orders?”

“Rem will eliminate with her own hands anything that could be an obstacle to the fulfillment of Master Roswaal’s dearest wish. You are merely one of those things.”

“Can’t he even discipline his pet dog? Try thinking about how a passerby feels getting bitten, huh?”

“Rem will not allow insults toward Master Roswaal.”

Subaru had lightly provoked her to probe her true feelings, and his cheek burst open.

His vision shook from the impact of the blow, and his hand involuntarily touched his cheek where the sharp pain was—it was wet with bright red blood.

She had used the chain—the connection to the iron ball still embedded in the wall—like a whip, striking the side of Subaru’s face with iron. His cheek was torn in the distorted pattern of the chain, and blood flowing from his forehead entered his left eye, stinging with pain.

All this damage from one smart-assed remark. But it was worth it for what he gleaned.

At least her loyalty to Roswaal was genuine. And it was likely true that she believed disposing of Subaru was for Roswaal’s sake.

It was judged that Subaru’s departure from the Roswaal Manor would be detrimental to Roswaal, who was supporting Emilia in the Royal Selection.

In short, when you put it all together, the heart of the matter was—

“Ah, so that’s it. —Did you really trust me that little?”

“Yes.”

She nodded without hesitation, and Subaru felt a pain as if a sharp blade had been thrust deep into his chest. That answer stirred up unpleasant imaginings for Subaru, and affirming those imaginings changed the color of every scene from the days leading up to this.

Therefore, Subaru did not voice the suspicion that had sprouted in his heart.

He merely twisted the corner of his mouth in self-mockery at his own comical stupidity.

“Serves me right. Thinking I was getting along so well… what a misunderstanding.”

“…Sister is…”

“I don’t wanna hear it! —Eat this!”

Screaming, the moment Rem showed a slight hesitation, Subaru thrust the cell phone he had hidden behind his waist forward—immediately, a white light tore through the darkness-sunken forest, creating a stagnation in Rem’s movement for just a split second.

“—Raaagh!”

“————!”

He dashed out, slamming a shoulder tackle into her small frame to blow her away.

Whatever the trick, Rem swung that violent device with impossible strength, but in a simple collision, Subaru had the advantage in physique and weight.

Hit by the full-force charge, her small body flew backward; she lost her balance and fell to the ground. He ran past her without a single glance, sprinting at full speed.

Gasping, forcing air into his lungs, he raced his thoughts and his legs.

If this was Rem’s independent decision, he could still formulate a plan to save his life. If he could run back to the mansion and negotiate directly with her employer, there should be a possibility.

But if Roswaal’s opinion aligned with Rem’s, then this was nothing but a foolish act of escaping the lion’s den only to run into the wolf’s.

“Even so… if it’s… Emilia.”

If it was that silver-haired girl who shone more brilliantly than anyone in his memories, there was no room for doubt.

If it was her, if it was her, if it was her—

—She, who was a central figure in the Royal Selection, and who might find Subaru’s existence the most troublesome of all?

“————!?”

The manifestation of anxiety suddenly surfacing in his heart. Realizing that it was his own voice, infinitely dark and cold, Subaru was struck by a shock like lightning.

Unmistakably, he himself, with his own voice, had doubted Emilia’s heart.

Subaru himself, who knew how straightforward she was, how hard she tried, and how she never hesitated to suffer loss for the sake of others, had doubted her.

If positions change, thoughts change.

Just as Rem was now, how could he say for sure that the other people in that mansion weren’t gunning for Subaru’s life?

In the first place, it was a mistake not to suspect an inside job at the time of his second death. It happened inside the mansion. Naturally, the easiest people to pull it off were those on the inside.

Blinded by superficial relationships, this was the result of overlooking the obvious.

Running frantically through the mountains in this unsightly state, unable to come up with a single decent breakthrough.

—What happened to strictly gathering information this time?

When the threat actually appeared in a form different from his expectations, he had no choice but to cling to life while coughing up his life force like this.

He had been arrogant. He had been naive. He had been shallow.

Breathing roughly, conquering the slope as if tumbling down it, what filled Subaru’s head was not a method to break the deadlock, but simply words of regret.

“What on earth… was I doing this for…!”

A whimper spilled out, and tears involuntarily blurred his vision.

His steps faltered, and as the forest suddenly broke, Subaru saw the night closing in on the open sky.

And then—

“—Huh?”

A blade of wind from a super-high altitude flashed—and blew away everything below Subaru’s right knee.

Watching the tip of his right leg bounce away with momentum, Subaru’s body completely lost its posture. His balance destroyed, the momentum of his run caused his body to tilt and crash into the ground. The impact caused the wound on his cheek to bleed again, and he slammed his shoulder hard against a tree; a dull sound echoed, and pain raced through him as if electrodes were jabbed directly into his brain. Above all,

“Aaaaaaagh! M-My leg, my 

leeeeeeeg

!!”

There was no pain—that was the terrifying sensation.

His right leg was gone from the knee down, the blown-off fragment having flown beyond the bushes. The wound vividly displayed pink flesh, and fresh blood sprayed out with a delay, as if only just realizing the amputation had happened. Simultaneously, the pain invaded his nerves with a delay.

“————————————————!!!!”

He clawed at the ground, screaming a grand agony that became voiceless.

Holding the wound, thrashing his body, his free right arm beat the ground, punched the tree, his fingernails peeling off magnificently, his consciousness boiling from the heat of it all.

He suffered, and suffered, and suffered, and suffered through it.

A sensation of himself being eroded, as if the pain were filing down his nerves and planing his brain directly. Blood was being lost at a tremendous rate with every second, which meant the direct disappearance of the source of Subaru’s life.

And there,

“Ah, Rem finally caught up.”

Swaying the skirt of her maid outfit, Rem appeared dragging her weapon.

She looked at Subaru rolling on the ground, took note of the missing right leg, and after a moment of silent contemplation, she nodded.

“It must hurt; it must be agonizing. Please wait a moment.”

Crouching down, Rem turned her white palm toward Subaru’s wound.

His throat was already parched from voiceless screaming, and the writhing pain had exhausted his stamina, leaving him no will to move.

Subaru moved his clouded vision, silently watching Rem’s movements. Then,

“Oh Mana of water, grant healing to this one.”

She murmured, and suddenly a soft, pale light was released from Rem’s palm.

The light gently covered the stump of Subaru’s right leg, and with that pale glow, it began to compensate for the pain and sense of loss.

Feeling the sign of healing in a sensation akin to an itch, Subaru dragged back his consciousness that had started to drift away, and stared at Rem’s face in astonishment.

The pain hadn’t vanished completely, but a surprise greater than the pain dominated Subaru.

At this stage, he didn’t understand the reason why Rem would heal him. Receiving Subaru’s gaze, a hint of a faint smile floated onto Rem’s features.

Finding a tiny, meager hope in that—

“If you were to die easily after surviving all that, Rem wouldn’t be able to ask what she needs to ask.”

Her following words made him realize that it had been a fleeting, overly foolish optimism.

Rem’s arm pulled back, the sound of chains rang out, and the iron ball flew.

It slammed into the ground right next to the upper body of the fallen Subaru. Seen up close, it was rugged, crude, and simply a violent device specialized solely for threatening life.

Rem had deliberately placed the iron ball where he could see it. Her true intent was conveyed clearly enough.

It was an easy-to-understand demonstration to let him know that she held his life in her hands.

Seeing Subaru’s eyes harbor resignation, Rem prefaced with “Now then,” and said,

“Rem will ask you. Are you part of a camp belonging to a candidate hostile to Lady Emilia?”

“…My heart is always on Emilia-tan’s side.”

The moment he said it, the slack chain struck Subaru’s upper body violently.

His undershirt, torn by branches along the way, ripped all too easily, and the skin beneath was carved with identical lacerations; Subaru’s scream echoed through the forest.

“Who hired you, and for how much?”

“For Emilia-tan’s smile… Priceless.”

With a flick of her wrist, the same treatment. While physically experiencing the skill to strike the exact same spot without a millimeter of error, he praised that proficiency with a scream of agony.

After that, similar questions and similar answers.

The sound of the chain rang out as many times as there were questions, followed by a grand chorus of groans and screams.

Every time his consciousness was about to be blown away, he was treated by Rem’s own healing magic—Subaru was put through an infinite hell loop of healing and violence.

His spirit was worn down, and his consciousness cut out sporadically many times. Yet, his heart alone did not yield to Rem’s treatment.

Perhaps tired of Subaru’s obstinate attitude, Rem suddenly looked up at the sky and muttered,

“Rem must return soon. Preparations for dinner will be delayed.”

“…Dinner, huh. I wonder… what’s on the menu… today…”

“Let’s see. How about a minced meat pie?”

As Rem pointedly rattled the chain to flaunt the iron ball’s presence, the best Subaru could do was respond, “Please spare me from being on the dinner table.”

At Subaru’s posture of cracking jokes to the very end, Rem finally expressed emotion with a sigh. She then fell silent, looking down at Subaru with eyes more devoid of emotion than ever before.

“—Are you affiliated with the Witch Cult?”

A word he had never heard before jumped out, and Subaru furrowed his brows in confusion.

What kind of situation here did that word correspond to? Not understanding Rem’s true intent, he withheld his answer. To such a Subaru, Rem said,

“Answer me. You are ‘one ensnared by the Witch,’ are you not?”

“…By the… Witch?”

“Don’t play dumb!”

Raising her voice as if enraged, Rem pierced Subaru with a gaze that felt somewhat sharp. Through all the scenes from their true first meeting to this taking of each other’s lives, that was the moment Rem bared her emotions for the first time.

On that white face that usually never lost its composure, a slight vermilion of anger appeared as Rem looked down on Subaru with evident murderous intent.

Targeted by a killing intent he had no recollection of earning, Subaru shook his head weakly.

“I don’t… know… To begin with, my family has been… non-religious for generations…”

“Still playing dumb. —Reeking of the Witch’s scent like that, claiming you are unrelated is beyond transparent.”

Rem swung her arm down in front of Subaru, twisting the corner of her lips into a look of rage. At that unprecedented expression of emotion, Subaru opened his eyes wide, feeling as if he had touched slightly upon her true nature.

“Even if Sister and everyone else doesn’t notice, Rem notices! That stench, that lingering scent of a sinner—Rem harbors nothing but disgust and revulsion for it.”

In front of the silent Subaru, Rem bit her lip so hard she looked like she might grind her teeth.

“Even when peeking at you conversing with Sister, Rem felt like she would go mad with anxiety and anger. The source of what happened to Sister, someone related to that… carefree and nonchalant, in a place important to Rem and Sister…”

Incoherent words were muttered like a grudge, and sighs of resentment were showered mercilessly upon Subaru.

“Because Master Roswaal said to treat you with hospitality, Rem watched and waited as well… But even just monitoring you is now too painful to bear. Even knowing Sister was only pretending to look after you, while she acted like you two were so close!”

As if spewing out all the hatred she had bottled up, Rem slammed her passion into Subaru to make up for her lack of emotion until now.

Having said her piece, shoulders heaving, she glared at Subaru with wrath in her eyes. Then, suddenly, those eyes widened in surprise.

That was because,

“—Why…?”

In front of Rem, who had voiced her hatred, Subaru was quietly shedding tears.

“I knew… it. …I kind of, guessed it.”

His throat hitched, and the hot things welling up passed through his eyelids one after another, falling to his cheeks. While shedding tears he couldn’t stop, Subaru spoke in a broken, tearful voice.

“I’m going through this, after all… I knew there was a catch to being treated so kindly. But… I didn’t want, to hear it.”

The two who had taught the basics of housework to Subaru, who couldn’t do anything.

Ram, who mocked Subaru for not knowing how to wear a butler’s uniform. Rem, who helped him get dressed while chiding her.

He was crap at handling knives and couldn’t even peel vegetables properly, but for some reason, Ram had patiently stayed with him and taught him. And Rem, too, would offer a share to Subaru, who struggled in the kitchen, every time a menu item was completed.

“I stopped cutting my hands when peeling veggies. I learned that you wash clothes differently depending on the material, and I’m still in the middle of learning how to clean…”

In just four days and another four days, he couldn’t hope for much more improvement than that.

But he had thought that if he overcame several four days, he could still learn more in the days beyond.

“Reading and writing… just the simple stuff, but I learned how. I read a fairy tale. Thanks to you two…”

“What… are you talking about?”

At Subaru’s voice, which sounded like delirium, Rem lowered her tone as if feeling creeped out. Subaru squeezed out a breath and looked up into her eyes.

“I’m talking about the things… you two gave me…”

“Rem has no memory of such things.”

“—Why don’t you remember!!”

At the sudden outburst of passion, Rem’s foot involuntarily took a step back.

Lifting his prone body, scratching the ground with his unbalanced upper body, Subaru howled, baring his teeth.

“Why do you all gang up and leave me behind…!? What did I do…!? What are you telling me to do…!?”

He couldn’t control his emotions. He knew it was an extreme misplacement of anger, but still, Subaru’s heart, his soul, couldn’t stop screaming.

Summoned to another world, driven into unreasonable corners, he had still gritted his teeth and gotten through it. But he was at his limit.

“What was wrong… what did I do wrong? …Why do you guys hate me so much…?”

“—Rem is.”

“I… lo… you guys—”

—An impact did not allow him to continue the words that followed.

His body tilted from the power of the surprise attack, and Subaru’s body slowly bumped into the tree behind him.

Hearing a rasping breath and the sound of overflowing water close by, Subaru’s gaze wandered. And he found the cause immediately.

His throat.

The right half of Subaru’s throat had been gouged out by something, and air and blood bubbles were gushing fiercely from the middle of his windpipe.

Before his eyes, he saw Rem’s face looking at the wound in dumbfounded wonder.

Seeing only that, Subaru’s eyes lost their light, rolling back into whiteness.

His voice did not continue. His consciousness, too, shut down as if the power was cut.

Fading away. There was no pain. Anger, sadness, even emotion vanished somewhere.

Only, at the very end,

“—Sister, you are too kind.”

He felt as if he heard just that, murmured in someone’s sorrowful voice.
